gen-gf-kavivanar-fs-plein: Relaxed and friendly, Kavivanar writes its headings with a hand-drawn line that never changes thickness. Plein follows in a plain sans, tidy and clear, giving each round letter a visible channel in.
gen-gf-kavivanar-fs-recia: Kavivanar does its best work with loose, hand-drawn bowls as heavy as the stems beside them. Recia, a text serif, is sharper, with faint modulation you only catch up close.
gen-gf-kavivanar-fs-spline-sans: Spline Sans feels contemporary and approachable, its curves leaving wide gaps before they meet the stems. Spline Sans under a handwritten Kavivanar heading would keep a long page light and friendly.
gen-gf-kavivanar-fs-synonym: Kavivanar writes in one casual stroke, with a lowercase s whose ends flare open like a quick wave. Synonym is the dependable half, a plain sans stripe of constant ink that lets the handwriting be the personality.
gen-gf-kavivanar-outfit: Outfit draws its curves like bent cable, finishing each one well before it closes, so the letters feel clean and approachable. And Kavivanar's hand-drawn, relaxed headings sit above it, giving the page a loose, friendly start.
gen-gf-kavivanar-plus-jakarta-sans: That open-ended s in Kavivanar, flaring at both ends, gives the heading a relaxed, hand-drawn charm. And Plus Jakarta Sans, a plain sans with monoline construction, supplies the precision that keeps the friendliness in check.
gen-gf-kavivanar-sora: Sora reads as precise and geometric, a plain sans whose curves turn corners without any pressure swell. And Kavivanar earns its keep when set big and short, where its relaxed hand-drawn stroke gets room.
gen-gf-kavivanar-space-grotesk: Space Grotesk builds each glyph from a ribbon of constant width, with counters that open like a cut reed. Over a longer stretch it reads smoothly, and Kavivanar adds a hand-drawn smile on top.
gen-gf-kelly-slab-fs-rowan: Kelly Slab is bold and commanding, with big open eyes on every e and a. And Rowan, a literary serif with a mild letterpress-slug thick-thin shift, softens the tone beneath it.
gen-gf-klee-one-fs-amulya: Casual pen-and-paper charm, with no thick-thin contrast from stem to terminal. Amulya, a contemporary sans with generous curve gaps, can take a modest body size, since its openings do the work that Klee One's handwriting would not.
